newsitem.title: USA: Racy cover causes flap over Harper's magazine.
newsitem.headline: Racy cover causes flap over Harper's magazine.

text.p: A partially bared breast on the cover of Harper's August issue created a bottleneck at its Wisconsin printer, but the issue was distributed Monday thanks to some arm-twisting by the magazine's publisher.

Quad/Graphics Inc. of Pewaukee raised questions about whether the racy cover, which showed a photograph of a woman with her breast partly exposed being hugged at a fancy party, and would pass U.S. postal guidelines.
The local post office began to study the situation in early July, but Harper's publisher John MacArthur went for help to Postmaster General Marvin Runyon and New York Democratic Sen. Daniel Moynihan.
"I called Washington and screamed," MacArthur told the Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel. "If that's pornography, then I'm an astronaut."
The cover photograph, taken in England, showed portions of the woman's breast and went with an essay about American sexual morality.
The issue went out on time, but 9,000 copies of the Canadian version were mailed with brown wrappers because of Canada's stricter postal regulations.
